method: A one-shot pg_cron command first unschedules itself in a committed transaction, then executes the real function/trigger operation and holds its transaction for 25 seconds. The foreground session waits to observe its advisory marker, records both backend PIDs, then performs the conflicting operation and measures server-side wait time. No schema changes or new extensions. All data belongs to one synthetic CI actor.
qualifications: Initial parallel execute_sql attempts serialized and do not count as concurrency proof.

Self-unscheduling causes cron.job_run_details to report job canceled. The case results independently verify distinct concurrent backend PIDs, actual lock waiting and committed row state; scheduler success status is not claimed.
These SQL checks use PostgreSQL actor postgres. Restricted client grants are separately checked; this is not an authenticated end-to-end HTTP/storage-object test.
No actual storage bytes were uploaded; private-bucket and RLS checks do not replace public-URL/signed-URL tests using real bytes.
No production mutations were made by this agent. Root separately applied immutable 4028 to production.

WITH before AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT clock_timestamp() AS started,(SELECT pid FROM pg_locks WHERE locktype='advisory' AND classid=0 AND objid=40280102 AND granted LIMIT 1) AS publisher_pid), action AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT 1/(publisher_pid IS NOT NULL)::int AS observed_lock,public.cancel_composer_upload('7ae0c2e6-4e07-cf6b-a481-e58c08a2e090','2a21c3e8-d37b-8b0e-7988-e694873a076c') AS cancellation FROM before) SELECT cancellation,observed_lock,publisher_pid,pg_backend_pid() AS cancellation_pid,extract(epoch FROM clock_timestamp()-started)*1000 AS elapsed_ms FROM action CROSS JOIN before;
